Bioparco di Roma.question: The _____ was Zoo in Rome, Italy.
Bioparco di Roma.fact: Bioparco di Roma is a 17-hectare (42-acre) zoological garden located on part of the original Villa Borghese estate in Rome, Italy.

Bioparco di Roma.subject: Indian Architecture
Bioparco di Roma.question: The zoo covered 12 hectares (30 acres) and was erected in the northern part of the Villa Borghese estate; it opened on 5 January _____
Bioparco di Roma.fact: The zoo covered 12 hectares (30 acres) and was erected in the northern part of the Villa Borghese estate; it opened on 5 January 1911.

Bioparco di Roma.subject: Indian Architecture
Bioparco di Roma.question: The zoo was designed by _____, who had already opened a zoo in Hamburg Stellingen
Bioparco di Roma.fact: The zoo was designed by Carl Hagenbeck, who had already opened a zoo in Hamburg Stellingen.

Bioparco di Roma.subject: Indian Architecture
Bioparco di Roma.question: The park was built in the same style as the zoo in _____: ditches and pits instead of bars, and generous green spaces
Bioparco di Roma.fact: The zoo was designed by Carl Hagenbeck, who had already opened a zoo in Hamburg Stellingen. The park was built in the same style as the zoo in Hamburg: ditches and pits instead of bars, and generous green spaces.

Bioparco di Roma.subject: Indian Architecture
Bioparco di Roma.question: Various park expansions were undertaken, and in _____, a further expansion was planned into the neighbouring red deer park
Bioparco di Roma.fact: Various park expansions were undertaken, and in 1926, a further expansion was planned into the neighbouring red deer park.

Bioparco di Roma.subject: Indian Architecture
Bioparco di Roma.question: In _____, the architect Raffaele De Vico began his work on the new areas, which were to hold two main attractions: the large aviary and the reptile house which opened in 1935
